content.comment_body: Hi, I'm looking for assistance because I've exhausted all options and still have trouble. I have a [product_name] controller and an operator unit connected via Ethernet cable, but the operator unit does not respond when the controller is running. I created a simple program involving an input, a flag (intended to change the backlight to red on the operator unit), and an output—while all functions seem to work except the backlight change. When I try to check the controller settings from the operator unit, I receive repeated errors: Error: Failed to submit. Any help would be appreciated!
Have you configured the operator unit settings by specifying the IP address of the controller? The operator unit can only communicate if it has the correct controller IP address set.
Could you explain how to set that up?
Please refer to the attached file.
I've tried all the options shown but the issue remains.
Does the operator unit have an assigned IP address?
This is what I have been attempting.
I recommend opening a support ticket. Sorry, I cannot provide further help, but maybe others in the forum can assist.

The video shows that the controller and operator unit are not in the same IP address range. For instance: Controller IP: XXX.YYY.ZZZ.iii Operator unit IP: XXX.YYY.ZZZ.iii Only the last segment should differ; the rest must be identical for proper communication.
I've tried keeping the main IP segments identical and still no success. This issue has been ongoing for three days.

Standard controller configuration: IP address 192.168.000.001 Subnet 255.255.255.000 Standard operator unit screen: IP address 192.168.000.002 Subnet 255.255.255.000 Both devices need IP addresses in the same series, for example: 192.168.000.xxxx. Make sure you set the configuration to output to the operator unit screen or both, using [product_name] software.
Could you please provide detailed step-by-step instructions?

Is there another device on your network, such as a laptop or PC, using the same IP address as either the controller or operator unit? Try connecting the controller and operator unit directly, and consider swapping cables in case there's a fault.
When I tested, only the controller and operator unit were connected. I have tried five different cables.
Is it possible to reset the controller or operator unit to factory settings?

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are facing persistent connectivity problems between a controller and operator display unit over Ethernet. Configuration of IP settings has not resolved the issue; the operator unit does not interact with the controller, including not triggering expected features such as backlight change. There is frustration with the troubleshooting process, repetitive errors, and lack of clear guidance within the interface.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward setup and flawless communication between controller and operator unit once basic configuration steps are complete. They also look for clear instructions to resolve connection failures and expect all device features, such as backlight control, to work reliably.
